entities.summary: Caesar Barrand Hull, DFC was a Royal Air Force (RAF) flying ace during the Second World War, noted especially for his part in the fighting for Narvik during the Norwegian Campaign in 1940, and for being one of "The Few"—the Allied pilots of the Battle of Britain, in which he was shot down and killed. From a farming family, Hull's early years were spent in Southern Rhodesia, South Africa and Swaziland. He boxed for South Africa at the 1934 Empire Games. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Caesar Hull's participation in the Battle of Britain and his subsequent death during the Norwegian Campaign had a significant impact on the Allied forces' ability to defend against German air power. His actions as part of 'The Few' contributed to the eventual defeat of Nazi Germany.
